exposure: Third- or fourth-degree perineal tear in the first delivery
outcome: Mode of delivery in subsequent pregnancies
Recurrence rate of third- or fourth-degree perineal tears
cohort: 639,402 primiparous women who had a singleton, term, vaginal live birth and a second birth
finding: Women with a history of third- or fourth-degree perineal tear in their first delivery have a five-fold increased risk of experiencing another tear in their subsequent vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The rate of elective cesarean at second birth was significantly higher for women with a previous third- or fourth-degree tear.
